text:
A: Hiya! Oh, hello, I'm Gemma. Can you hear me all right?
B: Yeah, fine. I'm Ioana.
A: Ioana. Sorry, am I saying that right? I always panic with names.
B: Yeah, that's right.
A: Oh, good. Where are you?
B: Burnt Oak. North West London.
A: I'm Beeston, just outside Nottingham. We came down to London at Easter, actually, did the Natural History Museum because my daughter's obsessed with dinosaurs at the minute, and it was absolutely heaving. I think I was more stressed than she was.
B: Yeah, it's always rammed. I don't really go into central.
A: No, I don't blame you. Erm, what do you do, if you don't mind me asking?
B: Lettings admin. At an estate agent's in Edgware.
A: Ooh, okay. So, like, showing people round flats?
B: No, the negotiators do viewings. I do the paperwork. Contracts, deposits, compliance. Making sure gas certificates are in date.
A: Oh, but that's the bit that actually matters, isn't it? I'm a pharmacy technician, so I'm sort of the same, I'm the one checking everything before it goes out, and nobody notices unless you get it wrong, do you know what I mean?
B: Yeah, exactly that. Nobody says thanks when the certificate's in date.
A: No! And then one thing slips and it's all "right, who did this?"
B: Yeah. Is that at a hospital?
A: Yeah, a big one in Nottingham. Three days a week. I love it, honestly, but I'm one of those people who goes home and lies awake going "did I check that dose twice?" Even when I know I did. Rob says I should just let it go, but it's somebody's nan, isn't it, it's not a spreadsheet. Sorry, that got a bit deep for minute two.
B: No, I do that. With deadlines. I'll wake up at three and think, did I register that deposit.
A: And had you?
B: Always. Every time.
A: [laughs] That's it, isn't it! What gets you to sleep, then?
B: Podcasts, mostly. True crime.
A: Oh my God, me too! Which is a terrible idea before bed, I know. Do you listen to Casefile?
B: Yeah. That one's good, it's properly researched.
A: Have you tried the one with the two women who drink wine and chat about murders? Erm, I can't remember what it's called. They're dead funny.
B: No, I don't like those ones, actually. They get the facts wrong and they laugh about victims. It kind of annoys me.
A: [laughs] Okay, fair. That's me told.
B: Sorry. I just think if you're doing it, do it properly.
A: No, you're right, to be fair. I'd say that about a prescription. Do you listen on the way to work?
B: On the bus, yeah. The 113. It's always late, so I get through loads.
A: I listen while I batch cook on a Sunday. Chopping onions and hearing about a body in a lake. Rob thinks I'm unhinged.
B: [laughs] My boyfriend thinks the same. He walks in and goes, "Is this another dead person?"
A: That's exactly what Rob says! Oh, we're going to run out of time and I've talked at you the whole way, sorry.
B: It's fine. Send me the wine one, I'll give it a go. Maybe.
